chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Aḥmad ibn al-Jahm al-Kharrāz, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, from some of his companions, who said:

I was behind Abī al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام on al-Ṣafā or on al-Marwah, and he was not adding to more than two phrases: “O Allah, I ask You for good opinion of You in every state, and sincerity of intention in reliance upon You.”

So this does not contradict the first report, because the first is to be understood as recommendation and encouragement, while this one is to be understood as indicating permissibility and lifting restriction.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: the hill of Ṣafā in the rites of hajj and ʿumrah
key_terms.حُسْنَ الظَّنِّ: having a good opinion and hopeful trust in Allah

ai.seo_question: What du'a did Imam Mūsā al-Kāẓim عليه السلام recite at al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, and does it show that brief supplication there is permissible?
ai.summary: This report describes a brief du'a recited by Imam Mūsā عليه السلام at al-Ṣafā or al-Marwah, asking Allah for good opinion of Him in every state and sincerity in tawakkul. The closing statement clarifies that the narration does not conflict with earlier reports recommending longer recitation, since that recommendation indicates desirability, while this report establishes permissibility.
